description: Supply Chain Attack via Dependency Confusion Attackers publish malicious packages to public repositories with names matching internal package names. When the build process attempts to resolve dependencies, it may fetch the malicious package instead of the intended internal package. An attacker observes internal package names from public build logs or repository information, then publishes malicious packages with matching names to npm. During the next build, CodeBuild pulls the malicious package, which could exfiltrate secrets or compromise the build process.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1195.001 - Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
recommendation: Implement private artifact repository and strict package source controls
recommendation: Lock dependency versions and implement integrity verification

description: Overly Permissive IAM Roles in Pipeline The pipeline uses roles with broad permissions, including AdministratorAccess for CloudFormation deployments. This violates the principle of least privilege and could allow an attacker who compromises the pipeline to gain extensive access to the AWS account. An attacker who compromises the build process could leverage the overly permissive IAM roles to create unauthorized AWS resources, access sensitive data, or establish persistence in the environment.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1078.004 - Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
recommendation: Implement least privilege IAM roles
recommendation: Implement role separation and environment isolation

description: Insecure Secrets Management in Build Process The build environment has broad access to secrets and lacks proper isolation between build stages. Environment variables and secrets could be exposed through build logs or artifacts. A compromised build script could exfiltrate secrets from SecretsManager or environment variables, potentially exposing sensitive credentials or configuration data.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1552.007 - Unsecured Credentials: Container API
recommendation: Implement secret scope limitation and isolation

description: Insufficient Pipeline Integrity Validation The pipeline lacks comprehensive integrity checks for artifacts between stages. While S3 versioning is enabled, there's no cryptographic verification of artifacts or dependencies. An attacker with access to the artifact bucket could modify deployment artifacts between the build and deployment stages, potentially injecting malicious code into the production deployment.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1565.001 - Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation
owaspTop10: A08:2021-Software and Data Integrity Failures
